title: CiliumNetworkPolicy can no longer match `reserved:init` labels (from 1.14.2)

detection.reason: read from the agent's Cilium projection (feature names, never the policy's values); needs Cilium collection switched on in Integrations

quote: `CiliumNetworkPolicy` cannot match the `reserved:init` labels any more.
remediation: Convert every CiliumNetworkPolicy that selects or allows `reserved:init` into a CiliumClusterwideNetworkPolicy (same rules, cluster-scoped resource) before upgrading. A namespaced policy that keeps the match stops applying to endpoints in the init identity, so traffic it allowed during endpoint initialisation is denied.
verifyCommand: kubectl get ciliumnetworkpolicies.cilium.io -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | select(tostring | test("reserved:init")) | "\(.kind) \(.metadata.namespace // "-")/\(.metadata.name)"'  # each row is a namespaced policy that still matches reserved:init

title: `tofqdns-min-ttl` default drops from 3600 s to 0 — DNS policy now honours upstream TTLs

detection.reason: the option's VALUE is not collected (cilium-config ships key names only); the 1.13 chart writes tofqdns-min-ttl: "3600" on every install and the 1.14 chart stops writing it, so the key's presence today says nothing about the upgraded value

quote: The default value of `--tofqdns-min-ttl` has changed from 3600 seconds to zero.
remediation: The 1.13 chart wrote `tofqdns-min-ttl: "3600"` by default; the 1.14 chart drops it unless Helm `dnsProxy.minTtl` is set, so after `helm upgrade` a toFQDNs policy expires an allowed IP at the upstream DNS TTL instead of after an hour. Applications that cache a resolved IP past its TTL and open NEW connections to it are then denied. If any of your workloads do that, set Helm `dnsProxy.minTtl=3600` before upgrading.
verifyCommand: kubectl get ciliumnetworkpolicies.cilium.io,ciliumclusterwidenetworkpolicies.cilium.io -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | . as $p | [(.spec // empty), (.specs[]?)] | map(((.ingress // []) + (.egress // []) + (.ingressDeny // []) + (.egressDeny // []))[]) | select(any(.[]; (.toFQDNs // []) | length != 0)) | $p | "\(.kind) \(.metadata.namespace // "-")/\(.metadata.name)"'  # each row is a policy with toFQDNs rules — the TTL change applies to them

title: CNI configuration file renamed to `05-cilium.conflist`

detection.reason: datapath / runtime behaviour — nothing in the collected inventory states it

quote: Cilium now writes its CNI configuration file to `05-cilium.conflist` in all cases
remediation: Tooling that reads, templates or deletes `/etc/cni/net.d/05-cilium.conf` on the nodes (node images, bootstrap scripts, other CNIs in chaining mode) must look for `05-cilium.conflist` instead; a stale `05-cilium.conf` left behind can be picked up first by the container runtime. Cilium chained to the AWS VPC CNI (`cni-chaining-mode: aws-cni`) is not affected: it already wrote `05-cilium.conflist` before 1.14.
verifyCommand: kubectl get daemonset -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(any(.spec.template.spec.containers[]?; .image | test("(^|/)cilium/cilium([:@]|$)"))) | "\(.metadata.namespace)/\(.metadata.name) \([.spec.template.spec.containers[].image] | join(","))"'  # each row is the Cilium agent that writes the CNI file on every node

title: ENI mode: operator now fetches EC2 adapter limits from the AWS API — needs `ec2:DescribeInstanceTypes`

detection.reason: the operator's IAM permissions are AWS-side

quote: The default value of `--update-ec2-adapter-limit-via-api` has changed from `false` to `true`.
remediation: In ENI IPAM mode the 1.14 operator fetches instance-type limits from the EC2 API: the call in the code is `ec2:DescribeInstanceTypes`, while the upstream note names `ec2:DescribeInstances` — make sure the operator's IAM role (or the node role it inherits) grants both; upstream says `AmazonEKSWorkerNodePolicy` usually covers it on EKS. Without it the operator cannot refresh adapter limits. To keep the old behaviour set `update-ec2-adapter-limit-via-api: "false"`.
verifyCommand: kubectl get configmap -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.name == "cilium-config") | .data | to_entries[] | select(.key | test("^(ipam)$")) | "\(.key)=\(.value)"'  # ipam=eni means the operator needs ec2:DescribeInstanceTypes and ec2:DescribeInstances

title: Egress Gateway policies now DROP traffic when no gateway node is found

detection.reason: cilium-config keys only (names, never values): an option passed on the agent or operator command line (extraArgs) or in a ConfigMap of another name is not scanned; the key is set when Egress Gateway is enabled

quote: Egress Gateway policies now drop matching traffic when no gateway nodes can be found.
remediation: Egress Gateway is enabled here. Before upgrading, make sure every CiliumEgressGatewayPolicy's `egressGateway.nodeSelector` matches at least one Ready node; on 1.14 traffic from the selected pods is dropped (it used to leave the cluster un-rerouted) whenever no gateway node matches — e.g. during a gateway node replacement.
verifyCommand: kubectl get ciliumegressgatewaypolicies.cilium.io -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | select(.) | "\(.kind) \(.metadata.namespace // "-")/\(.metadata.name)"'  # each row is an egress gateway policy whose node selector must keep matching a Ready node

title: Gateway API support needs the v0.6 CRDs (ReferenceGrant v1beta1)

detection.reason: reads the installed ReferenceGrant CRD's served versions

quote: If Gateway API feature is enabled, please upgrade related CRDs to v0.6.x.
remediation: Install the Gateway API v0.6.x (or newer) CRDs before upgrading Cilium; the installed ReferenceGrant CRD does not serve `v1beta1`, which Cilium 1.14's Gateway API controller reads.

gate.reason: only clusters with Cilium's Gateway API support enabled read these CRDs

title: CiliumNetworkPolicy `auth.type` renamed to `authentication.mode`

detection.reason: read from the agent's Cilium projection (feature names, never the policy's values); needs Cilium collection switched on in Integrations

quote: The attribute `auth.type` is renamed to `authentication.mode` in both Ingress and Egress rules in CiliumNetworkPolicy CRD. The old attribute name is no longer supported
remediation: Rewrite `auth: {type: …}` to `authentication: {mode: required|disabled|test-always-fail}` in every policy the command lists before upgrading; the 1.14 CRD no longer accepts `auth.type`.
verifyCommand: kubectl get ciliumnetworkpolicies.cilium.io,ciliumclusterwidenetworkpolicies.cilium.io -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | . as $p | [(.spec // empty), (.specs[]?)] | map(((.ingress // []) + (.egress // []) + (.ingressDeny // []) + (.egressDeny // []))[]) | select(any(.[]; .auth != null)) | $p | "\(.kind) \(.metadata.namespace // "-")/\(.metadata.name)"'  # each row is a policy still using auth.type

title: Cluster Mesh: upgrade the clustermesh-apiserver in every cluster before the agents

detection.reason: upgrade ordering across clusters

quote: Please upgrade the *clustermesh-apiserver* in all clusters before the Cilium agents
remediation: 1.14 agents clean up stale remote-cluster state after reconnecting; against an older clustermesh-apiserver that restarts, that causes brief drops to remote pods and global services. Upgrade the clustermesh-apiserver in ALL meshed clusters first, then the agents.
verifyCommand: kubectl get deploy -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(any(.spec.template.spec.containers[]?; .image | test("(^|/)cilium/clustermesh-apiserver([:@]|$)"))) | "\(.metadata.namespace)/\(.metadata.name) \([.spec.template.spec.containers[].image] | join(","))"'  # each row is a clustermesh-apiserver and its version

title: CIDR deny policies now take precedence over overlapping allow policies

detection.reason: read from the agent's Cilium projection (feature names, never the policy's values); needs Cilium collection switched on in Integrations

quote: Deny policies now always take precedence over allow policies.
remediation: Traffic that an overlapping CIDR allow policy used to let through despite a CIDR deny policy is DROPPED on 1.14. For each policy pair the command lists, confirm the deny is intended; narrow the deny CIDR where it is not.
verifyCommand: kubectl get ciliumnetworkpolicies.cilium.io,ciliumclusterwidenetworkpolicies.cilium.io -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | select([(.spec // empty), (.specs[]?)] | any((.ingressDeny // []) + (.egressDeny // []) | length != 0)) | "\(.kind) \(.metadata.namespace // "-")/\(.metadata.name)"'  # each row is a policy with deny rules — check the CIDR allows that overlap it

title: IPv6 on `cilium_host` now comes from the IPAM pool

detection.reason: datapath / runtime behaviour — nothing in the collected inventory states it

quote: IPv6 on `cilium_host` now is assigned from IPAM pool, rather than using the same IPv6 as native host interface
remediation: On dual-stack clusters, firewall rules, monitoring or routes that expect `cilium_host` to share the node's native IPv6 must be updated: after the upgrade it holds an IPAM-allocated address.
verifyCommand: kubectl get configmap -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.name == "cilium-config") | .data | to_entries[] | select(.key | test("^(enable-ipv6)$")) | "\(.key)=\(.value)"'  # enable-ipv6=true means cilium_host gets a new IPv6

title: `sockops-enable` and `force-local-policy-eval-at-source` removed

detection.reason: cilium-config keys only (names, never values): an option passed on the agent or operator command line (extraArgs) or in a ConfigMap of another name is not scanned

quote: The `sockops-enable` and `force-local-policy-eval-at-source` options deprecated in version 1.13 are removed.
remediation: Remove these keys from cilium-config (Helm `sockops.enabled`); 1.14 ignores them, so sockops acceleration silently stops.
verifyCommand: kubectl get configmap -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.name == "cilium-config") | .metadata.namespace as $ns | .data | to_entries[] | select(.key | test("^(sockops-enable|force-local-policy-eval-at-source)$")) | "\($ns)/cilium-config \(.key)=\(.value)"'  # each row is an option still set in cilium-config

title: `tunnel` option deprecated (removed in 1.15) — use `routing-mode` / `tunnel-protocol`

detection.reason: cilium-config keys only (names, never values): an option passed on the agent or operator command line (extraArgs) or in a ConfigMap of another name is not scanned; the 1.13 chart writes tunnel on every install and the 1.14 chart converts Helm `tunnel` itself

quote: The `tunnel` option is deprecated and will be removed in v1.15.
remediation: `helm upgrade` with the 1.14 chart rewrites `tunnel` into `routing-mode` / `tunnel-protocol` for you; only a hand-managed cilium-config must change. There, replace `tunnel` with `routing-mode: native` (was `tunnel: disabled`) or `routing-mode: tunnel` + `tunnel-protocol: vxlan|geneve` (Helm `routingMode` / `tunnelProtocol`). 1.15 drops `tunnel` entirely (rtz-cilium-1.15-tunnel-option-removed).
verifyCommand: kubectl get configmap -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.name == "cilium-config") | .metadata.namespace as $ns | .data | to_entries[] | select(.key | test("^(tunnel)$")) | "\($ns)/cilium-config \(.key)=\(.value)"'  # each row is an option still set in cilium-config
coversNotes: Helm Options: Following the deprecation of the `tunnel`

remediation: If cilium-config `ipam` is `cluster-pool-v2beta`, plan the move to `multi-pool` IPAM: 1.15 removes the mode (rtz-cilium-1.15-cluster-pool-v2beta-removed).

title: Hubble Relay `tls-client-*` / `tls-server-*` flags deprecated

detection.reason: hubble-relay's own config file values are not collected

quote: The following Hubble Relay options are deprecated and will be removed in v1.15:
remediation: If you run hubble-relay with hand-written flags, rename `tls-client-cert-file`/`tls-client-key-file` to `tls-hubble-client-*` and `tls-server-cert-file`/`tls-server-key-file` to `tls-relay-server-*`. Helm-managed relays are rendered correctly by the 1.14 chart.

title: `kube-proxy-replacement` values `strict` / `partial` / `disabled` deprecated — use `true` / `false`

detection.reason: the option's VALUE is not collected (cilium-config ships key names only); the chart writes kube-proxy-replacement on every install

quote: The `kube-proxy-replacement` option's values `strict`, `partial` and `disabled` are deprecated and will be removed in v1.15.
remediation: Set `kube-proxy-replacement` to `true` (was `strict`) or `false` (was `disabled`; with `partial`, also enable each kube-proxy-replacement feature you used explicitly). 1.15 still accepts the old values; 1.16 does not — its chart refuses to render and its agent refuses to start with them — and upstream ships no 1.16 note for it, so change the value now.
verifyCommand: kubectl get configmap -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.name == "cilium-config") | .data | to_entries[] | select(.key | test("^(kube-proxy-replacement)$")) | "\(.key)=\(.value)"'  # strict|partial|disabled must be rewritten

title: Hubble Relay `securityContext` now applies to the container and defaults to non-root, all capabilities dropped

detection.reason: Helm values are not collected

quote: The `securityContext` for Hubble Relay now applies to the container, not the pod.
remediation: If you set `hubble.relay.securityContext` expecting pod-level settings, move them to `hubble.relay.podSecurityContext`. Custom relay images that need root or capabilities must set them explicitly.

quote: Values `ipam.operator.clusterPoolIPv4PodCIDR` and `ipam.operator.clusterPoolIPv6PodCIDR` were deprecated in Cilium 1.11
remediation: Run `helm get values` for the Cilium release and rename before upgrading: `ipam.operator.clusterPoolIPv4PodCIDR` → `clusterPoolIPv4PodCIDRList` (same for IPv6) — the 1.14 chart refuses to render while the old names are set (`helm upgrade` fails), so nothing changes until you rename; `hubble.tls.ca*` → `tls.ca*`; drop `hubble.peerService.enabled` and `hubble.ui.securityContext.enabled`.

Helm Options: Value `hubble.ui.securityContext.enabled` was deprecated in Cilium
